sn45.4:1.2: Then, in the morning, the Venerable Ānanda dressed and, taking bowl and robe, entered Savatthī for alms.
sn45.4:1.3: The Venerable Ānanda saw the brahmin Jaṇussoṇi departing from Savatthī in an all-white chariot drawn by mares.
sn45.4:1.4: The horses yoked to it were white, its ornaments were white, the chariot was white, its upholstery was white, the reins, goad, and canopy were white, his turban, clothes, and sandals were white, and he was being fanned by a white chowry.
sn45.4:1.6: “Divine indeed, sir, is the vehicle! It appears to be a divine vehicle indeed,
sn45.4:2.1: Then, when the Venerable Ānanda had walked for alms in Savatthī and returned from his alms round, after his meal he approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, sat down to one side, and said to him: “Here, venerable sir, in the morning I dressed and,
sn45.4:3.1: taking bowl and robe, entered Savatthī for alms.
sn45.4:3.2: I saw the brahmin Jaṇussoṇi departing from Savatthī in an all-white chariot drawn by mares….
sn45.4:3.7: ‘Divine indeed, sir, is the vehicle! It appears to be a divine vehicle indeed, sir!’ Is it possible, venerable sir, to point out a divine vehicle in this Dhamma and Discipline?”
sn45.4:4.1: “It is possible, Ānanda,” the Blessed One said.
sn45.4:4.2: “This is a designation for this Noble Eightfold Path:
sn45.4:4.3: ‘the divine vehicle’ and ‘the vehicle of Dhamma’ and ‘the unsurpassed victory in battle.’
sn45.4:5.1: “Right view, Ānanda, when developed and cultivated, has as its final goal the removal of lust, the removal of hatred, the removal of delusion.
sn45.4:5.8: Right concentration, when developed and cultivated, has as its final goal the removal of lust, the removal of hatred, the removal of delusion.
sn45.4:6.1: “In this way, Ānanda, it may be understood how this is a designation for this Noble Eightfold Path:
sn45.4:6.2: ‘the divine vehicle’ and ‘the vehicle of Dhamma’ and ‘the unsurpassed victory in battle.’”
sn45.4:6.3: This is what the Blessed One said.
sn45.4:7.1: Having said this, the Fortunate One, the Teacher, further said this:
sn45.4:8.3: Shame is its pole, mind its yoke-tie,
sn45.4:9.2: Its axle jhana, energy its wheels;
sn45.4:10.2: and seclusion: These are the chariot’s weaponry,
sn45.4:10.4: As it rolls towards security from bondage.
sn45.4:11.1: “This divine vehicle unsurpassed Originates from within oneself.
sn45.4:11.3: The wise depart from the world in it,
